content:
support_jess: FYI — multiple customers reporting console graphs stuck on spinner + 500s from analytics API after the 23:40 deploy. Seeing ~30% of panel requests fail. Example error returned by analytics-api: 

support_jess: ```
curl -i -X POST https://analytics-api.internal/v1/query 
-H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' 
-d '{"query":"SELECT count(*) FROM metrics WHERE org_id=123"}' 

HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
Content-Type: application/json
{"error":"internal: query execution timeout", "trace_id":"trc_0a7b..."}
```

support_jess: Happening across regions (us-west, eu). Customer Tina (customer_ops_tina) says panels show stale data or no series at all. Opening thread to triage. @eng_luke can you take? :eyes:

eng_luke: taking this. Any recent infra changes besides the analytics-api deploy?

customer_ops_tina: nothing on our side. Repro steps from customer: 
1) Open dashboard "Revenue - hourly"
2) Click refresh
3) Panel spinner, chrome devtools shows 500 on POST /v1/query, no body refresh.
Trace ID they provided: trc_0a7b...

sre_maya: looking at infra metrics now. I see a jump in analytics-api outbound errors to clickhouse at 23:41 and query_queue_length spiked. Metrics: 
- analytics.query_queue_length: 512 -> 4096 (spike)
- analytics.api_500_rate: 0.02 -> 0.28
- clickhouse.conn_errors: 0.01 -> 0.12

sre_maya: hypothesis: query fanout/backpressure after a bad plan on latest model or change in batch size. Some consumers timed out and returned 500.

eng_luke: can we get the exact query that triggered the spike? customer_ops_tina, can you paste the panel query id or the raw query?

customer_ops_tina: panel raw query (redacted): 
```
{"query":"SELECT time_bucket(60, ts) as t, sum(val) FROM event_metrics WHERE org_id=123 AND metric='impressions' GROUP BY t ORDER BY t DESC LIMIT 360"}
```
They said the same query used to succeed but now returns 500s intermittently.

sre_maya: pulling analytics-api logs for trace_id trc_0a7b...
sre_maya: log excerpt: 
```
2026-03-17T23:41:03Z analytics-api ERROR trace=trc_0a7b ... worker.go:298 query execution failed: context deadline exceeded after 10s
2026-03-17T23:41:03Z analytics-proxy WARN connection pool exhausted: active=1024 max=1024
```
sre_maya: looks like connection pool exhaustion -> context deadline -> 500. The 10s deadline is the service default.

eng_luke: OK. Quick mitigation options: 
- increase analytics-api connection pool temporarily
- bump query timeout from 10s -> 30s (risk: higher latency overall)
- enable front-end cached snapshot fallback for panels for 5m
- throttle expensive queries at proxy layer

devex_omar: front-end can flip to cached snapshots ASAP. Minimal change: if resp.status >= 500 show last successful snapshot with a small banner. I can ship a client-side flag. Snippet: 
```js
if (resp.status >= 500) { showCachedSnapshot(panelId) }
```

support_jess: customers want quick fix, caching would reduce user-visible errors. But we should also address backend pool exhaustion so downstream doesn't accumulate.
\
incbot: Deploybot: rollback flag is available for analytics-api v3.2. Would you like me to rollback the last release? :robot_face:

eng_luke: Not yet. Let's try connection-pool bump + restart analytics-api pods in us-west first. @sre_maya please: 1) increase max connections to 2048 2) restart a subset (canary) 3) monitor error rate for 5m.

sre_maya: doing step 1 and rolling restarts now (canary 2 pods). Watchlist: analytics.api_500_rate, clickhouse.conn_errors, query_queue_length.

(5m pass)

sre_maya: canary looks good, 500 rate down to 0.06, queue length slowly falling. Rolling remainder now.

deploybot: incbot: analytics-api pods rolling restart initiated by sre_maya at 23:49 UTC.

customer_ops_tina: customer confirms some panels are loading now, but one dashboard still shows missing series for older buckets.

eng_luke: that could be partial due to in-flight queries dropped during restarts. Can you ask customer to refresh after 2 minutes? Also capture any new trace ids if they still see 500s.

customer_ops_tina: they refreshed, panels recovered for the most part. They saw one more 500 with trace trc_0a7bX2 then nothing.

eng_luke: we'll keep monitoring for the hour. Root cause likely query fanout spike combined with conservative connection pool and low timeout. Action items: 
- sre_maya: make pool max conn change config commit (temporary) and prepare a safe gradual rollout config PR to increase pools and add backpressure metrics (ETA 2h)
- eng_luke: create a follow-up to tune analytics query planner/limits; consider smarter batching and TTLs for expensive panels (ETA 1 week)
- devex_omar: implement client-side cached snapshot fallback behind feature flag (ETA 2h)

sre_maya: created PR #4382 to bump pool and add metrics. Will revert to original values after full fix is deployed or make permanent post-review.

eng_luke: marking as incident P2 for tracking. Will add postmortem if we see recurrence.

support_jess: informing affected customers and updating status page note that graphs may have degraded performance due to analytics throttling — link to status update: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/abcd1234

customer_ops_tina: customer appreciated the prompt response. They want to be notified when permanent fix is deployed.

eng_luke: noted. Closing thread once all action items are complete. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
